document.title: Update, Islamic Extremist Terrorist Threat
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Central Intelligence Agency 9/11 File: Hundreds of Secret Agency Documents on Osama Bin Laden Declassified
document.note: [Top Secret] Top Secret briefing to the DCI. Says disruption operations against the Millennium plot "bought time… weeks… months… but no more than one year" before al-Qaeda would strike. Cited in 9/11 Commission Report Chapter 6, Endnote 55.

persons.name: Usama bin Ladin
persons.role: Leader of the Islamic extremist terrorist threat; target of CIA operations
persons.status_detail: Alive and being targeted as of January 2000

persons.name: Ahmad Shah Masood
persons.role: Afghan opposition commander; the CIA was reviewing the Afghan situation around him

organizations.name: Central Intelligence Agency
organizations.notes: Author of the briefing. The slide says operations conducted by the CIA and foreign services disrupted terrorist plans.

organizations.name: Director of Central Intelligence
organizations.notes: Issued a message that the threat was a top priority.

places.name: Afghanistan

events.description: The Millennium celebrations were intended as the 'kick off' for a possible period of extended terrorist attacks. Terrorists delayed their plans because of extensive disruption operations conducted by the CIA and foreign services.
The Millennium celebrations were intended as the 'kick off' for a possible period of extended terrorist attacks. This is the briefing's assessment of the planned attacks.
CIA and foreign services conducted extensive disruption operations. The terrorists delayed their plans as a result, which bought time of 'weeks or months' but not more than one year.
The CIA briefing 'Update, Islamic Extremist Terrorist Threat' was produced. It lists increased activity, the DCI message, targeting UBL, and a relook at the Afghan situation including Masood.

relationships.detail: The CIA lists targeting UBL as an action item in its response to the threat.
The DCI sent a message directing the Agency's counterterrorism effort.
The slide lists a relook at the Afghan situation, with Masood named beneath it. This suggests a review of CIA engagement with Masood.
Masood is named under the heading about the Afghan situation.
CICTC appears on the CIA's list of counterterrorism actions. The slide text about its funding is garbled.

key_claims: The CIA assessed that the Millennium celebrations were intended as the start of a possible period of extended terrorist attacks.
Terrorists delayed their plans because of extensive disruption operations by the CIA, other agencies and foreign services.
The disruption bought time of weeks or months, but probably no more than one year.
The CIA responded with a DCI message, more personnel working the issue, funding for the counterterrorism center, a review of the Afghan situation (including Masood), and targeting UBL.
